english: Let $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$ be three non-coplanar vectors and let $x$ be a real number with $0<x<1$. The volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges $\overrightarrow{a}+x\overrightarrow{b}+x^2\overrightarrow{c}$, $\overrightarrow{b}+x\overrightarrow{c}+x^2\overrightarrow{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{c}+x\overrightarrow{a}+x^2\overrightarrow{b}$ is $\dfrac{49}{64}$ times the volume of the parallelepiped with coterminous edges $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$. Then the value of $x$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$ तीन असमतलीय सदिश हैं तथा $x$ एक वास्तविक संख्या है जहाँ $0<x<1$ है। सहकोटिक (coterminous) कोरों $\overrightarrow{a}+x\overrightarrow{b}+x^2\overrightarrow{c}$, $\overrightarrow{b}+x\overrightarrow{c}+x^2\overrightarrow{a}$ तथा $\overrightarrow{c}+x\overrightarrow{a}+x^2\overrightarrow{b}$ वाले समान्तर षट्फलक का आयतन, सहकोटिक कोरों $\overrightarrow{a}$, $\overrightarrow{b}$, $\overrightarrow{c}$ वाले समान्तर षट्फलक के आयतन का $\dfrac{49}{64}$ गुना है। तब $x$ का मान ______ है।
solution: Writing the edges in the basis $\overrightarrow{a},\overrightarrow{b},\overrightarrow{c}$: $[\overrightarrow{u}\ \overrightarrow{v}\ \overrightarrow{w}]=\Delta\,[\overrightarrow{a}\ \overrightarrow{b}\ \overrightarrow{c}]$ with
$C_1\to C_1+C_2+C_3$ and taking out $1+x+x^2$, then $R_2\to R_2-R_1$, $R_3\to R_3-R_1$:
solution_full: For vectors written in the basis $\overrightarrow{a},\overrightarrow{b},\overrightarrow{c}$, the box product is the determinant of the coefficients times $[\overrightarrow{a}\ \overrightarrow{b}\ \overrightarrow{c}]$:
Since $[\overrightarrow{a}\ \overrightarrow{b}\ \overrightarrow{c}]\neq0$, the ratio of the volumes is $|\Delta|$.
Each row sums to $1+x+x^2$. Applying $C_1\to C_1+C_2+C_3$ makes every entry of the first column $1+x+x^2$; taking this factor out leaves first column $(1,1,1)^T$.
The second gives $x^3=\dfrac{15}{8}>1$, impossible for $0<x<1$. The first gives $x^3=\dfrac18$, so $x=\dfrac12=0.5$.
originality_note: New: a parallelepiped whose edges are cyclic combinations a + x b + x^2 c, ..., so the volume ratio is a circulant determinant that factorises by row-sum and row operations into (1 - x^3)^2 (way 5). Closest known: edges a + b, b + c, c + a giving twice the volume. Different because: the coefficient matrix carries a parameter and its factorisation by determinant properties is the key step; the ratio then fixes x.

concept_use.Questions based on parallelopiped: Volumes of the two parallelepipeds as absolute values of box products, related by the coefficient determinant.
concept_use.Application of properties of determinant: C1 -> C1 + C2 + C3, taking out the common factor and row operations factorise the circulant determinant as (1 - x^3)^2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every vertex, vector and parameter is introduced before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently with sympy, is unique and equals the Answer Plan. The restriction 0 < x < 1 removes the second root x = (15/8)^(1/3); numerically confirmed the ratio 49/64 with random non-coplanar a, b, c at x = 0.5. Changed: no change.
key_step: Factorising the circulant coefficient determinant into (1 - x^3)^2 using determinant properties.
justification: Two linked ideas: box product of linear combinations equals the coefficient determinant times [a b c], and a parametric determinant factorised by properties; a sign choice finishes it. Comparable to 2021-P1-Q19 (L3) and below 2025-P2-Q12 (L4), which needs a coplanarity condition with two unknowns.
